blocks.text: Loading and failure are two outcomes of the same operation, so their boundaries usually sit together. The error boundary goes outside, because a chunk that fails to download throws rather than suspends.

items: A root boundary so nothing ever renders a blank page.
A boundary per route and per independent widget.

blocks.text: Where you put boundaries decides how much of the screen a single failure takes with it.

items: One boundary at the root, so a total failure still shows a branded page rather than a blank screen.
One per route, so navigating away recovers naturally.
One around each independent widget - a chart, a feed, a third-party embed - so one failure does not remove the rest of the page.

blocks.text: A boundary that only ever shows a dead end is frustrating. Give the user a way out, and reset the boundary's state so children can try again.
Give the boundary a `key` tied to the route or the record id. Navigating then remounts it with fresh state, so a user is never stuck on an error page for content they have moved away from.
`componentDidCatch` is where errors reach your monitoring tool. Include the component stack - it tells you which component failed, which the JavaScript stack often does not.
Never show a raw stack trace to users. It is noise to them and can leak internal details. Log the detail, show a plain message.
